suggestion.title: npm Package Installation with Unexpected Outbound Blockchain Traffic
suggestion.rationale: Article describes ChainDrop as self-propagating worm via npm packages using Ethereum smart contracts for C2 routing. Pipeline failed to generate any detection for installation-time execution or anomalous network patterns to blockchain infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor build/dev environments for npm install processes initiating outbound connections to Ethereum RPC endpoints or blockchain nodes (e.g., Infura, Alchemy). Look for post_install or preinstall scripts spawning curl/wget to web3 protocol handlers. Establish baseline of expected blockchain traffic and alert on new destinations.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Environment Secret Exfiltration via HTTP/DNS
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions extraction of GitHub Actions runner secrets; pipeline generated no detection for credential access phase. This is a core attack vector for supply-chain expansion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any GitHub Actions runner process (actions/runner@*) that reads environment variables matching patterns like GITHUB_TOKEN, *_TOKEN, *_SECRET and subsequently makes HTTP requests or DNS queries with base64/URL-encoded values in query parameters or POST bodies. Correlate with unusual destination IPs or domains outside trusted CI/CD infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Dependency Confusion Attack via Local npm Registry Override
suggestion.rationale: Self-propagating npm worm implies horizontal spread through shared dependencies and registry poisoning. Pipeline did not surface detection for typosquatting or registry-override attack vectors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor .npmrc file modifications in user home directories and project roots for registry redirects pointing to non-standard hosts. Detect npm install commands targeting packages with names similar to internal/popular packages (Levenshtein distance <2). Alert on installations where version numbers jump unexpectedly or pre/post-install scripts are added to previously clean package versions.

suggestion.title: Ethereum Smart Contract Interaction from CI/CD Runner
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies blockchain-based C2 via smart contracts; pipeline mapped zero command-and-control detection. This represents a novel evasion technique requiring specific blockchain protocol monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline Ethereum RPC calls and smart contract ABIs contacted by development/CI environments. Alert on new contract interaction patterns, particularly ethers.js or web3.js library usage in build logs combined with network connections to Ethereum mainnet/testnet nodes. Look for hardcoded contract addresses or ABI URLs in downloaded npm packages.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Poisoned Dependency Across Repository Network
suggestion.rationale: Self-propagating worm implies cross-repository infection via shared internal dependencies. Pipeline did not flag horizontal spread detection for monorepo or workspace-based npm installations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install commands across multiple repositories/workspaces on shared CI runners for installation of identical malicious transitive dependency versions within short time windows. Flag if a single compromised package version appears in lock files across multiple projects owned by different teams. Correlate with outbound connections to same C2 infrastructure from different runner instances.

suggestion.title: npm Package Publish Activity from Compromised CI/CD Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Self-propagating behavior implies automated re-publishing of poisoned packages or new variants. Pipeline generated zero detection for malicious package publication or registry manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm publish API calls from CI/CD runners outside official release pipelines. Alert on publish requests that include preinstall/postinstall script modifications or new dependencies added to package.json. Cross-reference npm registry audit logs for package versions published from unusual IP ranges or at atypical hours. Flag version bumps that skip expected semantic versioning patches.

suggestion.title: Vishing + Adversary-in-the-Middle Phishing for Session Tokens
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes UNC6671 contacting employees on personal phones, spoofing help desk, directing to fake domains hosting 'adversary-in-the-middle phishing kits designed to steal credentials and session cookies in real time.' This multi-stage social engineering attack is core TTP missed entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for phishing emails or SMS referencing MFA/passkey enrollment or password updates, directing to domains mimicking corporate identity. Correlate with vishing call reports (ticketing system, employee surveys). Alert on credential submission to non-corporate domains; flag AitM patterns (certificate mismatches, cookie exfiltration attempts).

suggestion.title: Okta/Microsoft 365 SSO Dashboard Abuse After Credential Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'after stealing Microsoft 365 or Okta single-sign-on accounts, the attackers log into the SSO dashboard, which gives access to all the cloud platforms that are linked to the account.' Represents credential_access→lateral_movement into centralized cloud identity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Okta or O365 logins from anomalous geoIP/ASN, followed by immediate enumeration of SSO dashboard apps or token refresh storms. Flag logins without expected MFA step or from impossible-travel IPs. Monitor for session token creation across multiple cloud platforms in rapid succession post-login.

suggestion.title: Automated Bulk Data Exfiltration Across Multiple Cloud Services
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'hackers then use automated tools to steal data from all cloud services they gain access to.' This indicates rapid, scripted access to all platforms linked via single SSO compromise—distinct from targeted single-app theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on single user account accessing and downloading large volumes from multiple cloud services (Salesforce, Slack, Confluence, etc.) within 10-30 minute window. Flag bulk export operations (all-users reports, database dumps) preceded by SSO token reuse. Monitor for scripted API calls across disparate platforms from single source IP.

suggestion.title: Systematic Deletion of Security Notifications and Password-Reset Emails
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'delete security notifications and password-reset emails from compromised inboxes.' This is a specific defense-evasion tactic to prevent detection and disable recovery options post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor mailbox AuditLog for bulk deletion of emails from system accounts (Azure AD notifications, Office 365 alerts, password management services). Alert on deletion of messages containing keywords: 'security', 'alert', 'suspicious', 'password reset', 'verify identity' shortly after account compromise indicator (first login anomaly). Flag deletions performed via PowerShell or unusual client.

suggestion.title: Help Desk Spoofing Requests for MFA/Passkey Re-enrollment
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes UNC6671 'contact[ing] employees on their personal mobile phones while spoofing corporate help-desks and claiming that workers need to enroll in passkeys or update their multi-factor authentication settings.' This is the initial-access vehicle.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate vishing reports (employee-reported suspicious calls claiming to be IT) with phishing emails/SMS sent same day to same cohort. Monitor for MFA re-enrollment campaigns not initiated by helpdesk ticketing system. Alert on requests to enroll in passkeys or MFA to external URLs or unfamiliar domains. Flag bulk outreach claiming urgent security updates.

suggestion.title: Cloud Service Discovery and Enumeration Post-SSO Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article notes attackers log into SSO dashboard to gain 'access to all the cloud platforms that are linked to the account.' Implies discovery phase scanning available apps tied to compromised identity before selective or bulk exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid sequential API calls to enumerate cloud apps, app catalogs, or accessible services immediately post-login to SSO dashboard. Flag access to Okta Catalog API or O365 discovery endpoints within minutes of anomalous login. Monitor for enumeration patterns (attempting access to 10+ distinct cloud services with matching timestamp deltas) by single account.

suggestion.title: KVM Guest-to-Host Escape Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'privileged L1 guest code escape to Linux hosts'—describes privilege escalation via hypervisor boundary violation. Pipeline generated no use cases for this attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on guest-spawned processes attempting direct hardware access, ioctl calls to KVM device files from elevated guest contexts, or attempts to map guest memory regions to host space. Monitor for abnormal vcpu exit handlers or attempts to abuse KVM-specific syscalls.

suggestion.title: Suspicious KVM Kernel Module Interaction
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is in KVM kernel module itself. Article phrase 'KVM Flaw' indicates kernel-level exploitation. No detection logic for KVM-specific module abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect loading of KVM modules after initial compromise, suspicious open/close of /dev/kvm from non-qemu processes, or ioctl sequences known to exploit KVM state machine. Alert on attempts to read/write KVM vCPU state outside normal hypervisor operation.

suggestion.title: Hypervisor Escape via Memory Mapping Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Guest escape attacks typically exploit memory management. Article indicates L1 guest (nested hypervisor / privileged guest) can escape—memory isolation failure. No use case for detecting memory mapping abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for guests attempting mmap of privileged memory regions, requests for page table modifications outside guest scope, or side-channel probing patterns (Spectre/Meltdown-style) targeting host kernel. Flag attempts to establish cross-VM communication channels.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation from Guest Administrator to Host Root
suggestion.rationale: Attack path is explicit: privileged (admin-level) guest code → host escape. No detection use case for this specific escalation vector within virtualized environments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In hypervisor host OS, detect spawning of processes or opening of resources initiated from guest VM contexts with privileges elevating beyond guest boundary. Monitor for unexpected process creation triggered by KVM process, especially those gaining host-level capabilities.

suggestion.title: Traefik ReplacePathRegex configuration audit — unsanitized capture groups
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability requires 'regex that captures user-controlled path segments without a mandatory separator (for example `regex: "^/api(.*)"`, `replacement: "/$1"`)'. No UC hunts for this dangerous pattern in traefik.yml or dynamic.yml configs.
log_sources: Web access logs with traefik config paths
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for traefik YAML configs (dynamic.yml, traefik.yml, traefik.toml) containing ReplacePathRegex middleware where replacement uses $1/$2 capture groups without explicit path separators (e.g., `replacement: "/$1"` without delimiter validation). Compare against baseline configurations.

suggestion.title: Traefik middleware chain bypass — successful auth re-entry on path-traversal request
suggestion.rationale: Article describes traversal bypassing auth middleware entirely. No UC explicitly hunts for request pairs: (1) legitimate request denied by auth middleware (401/403), (2) traversal variant of same endpoint succeeds (2xx) — the actual bypass signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlation: same source sends request to `/admin` → 403, then `/api/../admin` or `/../admin` → 200/302 within 60 seconds. Indicates successful middleware bypass chain on same Traefik instance.

suggestion.title: Traefik version fingerprint in error responses — CVE-2026-65600 affected versions
suggestion.rationale: Article does not specify patched vs. vulnerable versions, but operational security hunt would fingerprint Traefik version from HTTP Server headers, error messages, or Traefik dashboard exposure to identify at-risk instances before detection of actual exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP responses with Server: traefik/X.Y.Z headers or Traefik dashboard exposure (typical port 8080 or 8081, path /dashboard or /ping). Correlate version against known-vulnerable range for CVE-2026-65600.

suggestion.title: Protected route access pattern change post-traversal — new source accessing admin/internal routes
suggestion.rationale: Article describes auth bypass enabling access to protected routes (implied: admin panel). No UC hunts for behavioral change: source IP suddenly accessing previously-denied admin endpoints after traversal probe attempt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline: track which sources access `/admin`, `/internal`, `/api/admin` → see 403/401. Alert if same source later accesses these routes with 2xx response after prior traversal attempt (`%2e%2e`, `/../` patterns) within 10-minute window.

suggestion.title: Interrupt Descriptor Table (IDT) or Interrupt Handler Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Interrupt Injection Attack' — this is the primary attack vector. Pipeline generated zero UCs for interrupt handler interception or IDT manipulation despite this being core to the threat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unprivileged process access to IDT registers, exception handler vectors, or kernel-mode interrupt controller memory regions. Alert on allocation of code at addresses matching exception handler entry points or modification of saved exception handler pointers.

suggestion.title: IBRS/IBPB/STIBP MSR Tampering or Disabling
suggestion.rationale: Article states attack 'bypasses Spectre v2 defenses' — Spectre v2 mitigations are implemented via MSR 0x48, 0x49, 0x4B writes. Pipeline failed to generate detection for MSR manipulation or mitigation disabling.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag WRMSR instructions targeting Spectre v2 MSRs (IBRS=0x48, IBPB=0x49, STIBP=0x4B) from user-mode contexts. Monitor for repeated MSR reads followed by modified writes that indicate speculative execution state manipulation.

suggestion.title: Speculative Execution Probe via Exception-Based Timing Side Channel
suggestion.rationale: Interrupt injection facilitates speculative execution exploitation; article premise is bypassing existing Spectre v2 defenses. Pipeline missed detection for exception-generation loops used to measure cache/timing behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect high-frequency exception generation (divide-by-zero, page fault loops) used to build timing oracles. Alert on tight loops executing privileged instructions that read/modify CPU speculation controls (SPEC_CTRL, ARCH_CAPABILITIES).

suggestion.title: Cross-Core Interrupt or IPI-Based Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Interrupt injection on multi-core systems (mentioned: 'Intel and AMD CPUs') enables lateral code execution. Pipeline created zero UC for inter-processor interrupt (IPI) abuse or multi-core attack coordination.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes generating or receiving IPI sequences, accessing inter-processor communication channels, or correlating exception spikes across multiple CPU cores. Flag unusual CPU_PAUSE instruction sequences used to synchronize multi-core attacks.

suggestion.title: Kernel-Mode Callback or Exception Handler Hooking via Interrupt Mechanism
suggestion.rationale: Interrupt injection can redirect kernel exception handlers. Pipeline failed to model detection for syscalls registering/modifying kernel callbacks or exception-handler redirection via interrupt table manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on user-mode processes calling syscalls that register exception handlers (signal() on Unix, SetUnhandledExceptionFilter on Windows). Correlate with memory allocations and code writes targeting exception-handler memory regions.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Agent Polling Protocol Access
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector explicitly specified as 'unauthenticated remote code execution via the agent polling protocol.' Article does not specify authentication requirement, suggesting protocol accepts unauthenticated payloads. Phrase: 'unauthenticated remote code execution via the agent polling protocol'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound connections to TeamCity agent polling protocol endpoints (typically port 9090 or custom agent port) from external/untrusted networks. Flag connection attempts that do not present valid TeamCity agent credentials or certificates. Correlate with process execution events on the TeamCity server.

suggestion.title: Java Deserialization RCE via TeamCity Agent
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is 'deserialization of untrusted data' leading to 'remote code execution.' This is a Java serialization gadget chain attack pattern. Phrase: 'deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability that could allow unauthenticated remote code execution'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Java process logs and network traffic from TeamCity agent processes for indicators of serialized object deserialization attacks (ObjectInputStream, gadget library references, CommonsCollections, etc.). Alert on unexpected child processes spawned from TeamCity JVM after agent polling connections. Signature-match for common Java deserialization payloads.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Process Execution Anomaly Detection
suggestion.rationale: RCE via agent polling results in arbitrary code execution in the context of TeamCity agent/server processes. Article implies post-compromise execution environment. Need to detect suspicious process execution spawned from TeamCity contexts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when TeamCity agent or server processes (java.exe with -Dteamcity flag, teamcity-agent.exe, etc.) spawn unexpected child processes, especially: cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, python, or processes not in TeamCity whitelist. Validate parent-child relationships against baseline. Prioritize rare or never-before-seen commands.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Directory/Registry Tampering Post-RCE
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation results in RCE; attacker gains ability to modify TeamCity configuration, install persistence, or stage lateral-movement tools. File/registry changes in TeamCity home directory indicate compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor writes/modifications to TeamCity installation directory (typically C:\\ProgramData\\JetBrains\\TeamCity, /opt/teamcity, etc.) and registry keys (HKLM\\Software\\JetBrains\\TeamCity). Flag: new plugins, config.xml modifications, JAR/ZIP uploads, or batch scripts in plugins directory. Cross-correlate with suspicious process execution.

suggestion.title: Agent Polling Protocol Behavioral Anomaly (Network Signature)
suggestion.rationale: Agent polling protocol is a specific, structured communication channel. RCE exploitation will produce malformed or anomalous payloads. Phrase: 'via the agent polling protocol' implies protocol-level detection is viable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of valid TeamCity agent polling protocol traffic (payload sizes, intervals, authentication handshake patterns). Alert on: oversized payloads, rapid request spikes, protocol violations (malformed headers), or traffic from non-agent IP ranges. Correlate with IDS signatures for Java serialization attacks.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Agent Polling Protocol Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated remote code execution via the agent polling protocol' as the attack vector. No use case generated for detecting agent protocol abuse.

TeamCity agents should only poll from known internal build systems; unsolicited external agent connections indicate exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: TeamCity RCE via Java Deserialization Payload

Correlate with exception logs containing 'ObjectInputStream' or deserialization errors. RCE post-exploitation should show process creation originating from TeamCity JVM.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-63077 Vulnerability Scan & Patch Lag Detection

suggestion.title: Agent Polling Protocol Connection Anomalies & Timing Abuse

Flag POST requests to agent endpoints with: (a) inter-arrival time <1min (burst attack), (b) source IPs never seen polling before, (c) requests outside of normal build window times. Correlate with failed authentication attempts or exception logs.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-63077 Vulnerability Scanner Match

suggestion.title: TeamCity Agent Polling Protocol Anomalies

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual agent polling traffic to TeamCity servers: requests from unexpected source IPs, non-standard ports, or abnormal payload sizes. Look for serialized Java object signatures (AC F0 ED in hex) in polling protocol streams.

suggestion.title: Deserialization Attack: Java Gadget Chain Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'deserialization of untrusted data' as the vulnerability mechanism — the exploit path is Java object gadget chain execution, standard for this class of flaw.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamCity process (java.exe or java) for sudden child process spawning, shell invocations (cmd.exe, /bin/bash), or outbound connections immediately after incoming polling requests. Correlate with presence of common gadget libraries (ysoserial, commons-collections) in TeamCity lib directories.

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution via TeamCity: Process Execution Chain

suggestion.title: DNS Response Spoofing from Unauthorized Resolvers

suggestion.title: Out-of-Path Packet Injection (TCP Data Stream Corruption)
